title: My brother took the walkie-talkie to the barn. Then he knocked on the front door.
story:
My brother's voice came through the walkie-talkie, low and shaking. "Whatever knocks, don't open the door."

The power had died at our grandpa's farm, and the fog was so thick I couldn't see the porch rail. My brother took the flashlight and the second radio and went out to restart the generator in the barn. He hates radio talk. Calls it playing soldier. He never says over. Not once, not ever.

Ten minutes later, the radio crackled. "Something's out here. It walks like a person. Stay inside. Over."

Then three hard knocks on the front door.

"It's me," my brother said through the wood. "Open up, I dropped the radio. It's right behind me!"

I backed away from the door. I lifted the walkie to my mouth. "Are you still in the barn?"

"Still in the barn," it answered, calm. "Don't let it in. Over."

The knocking turned to pounding. My brother was screaming my name now, begging. Then it stopped, all at once, and something dragged across the porch and away into the fog.

The house went silent. The walkie crackled one last time.

"Good. Just us now. Over."
premise: brother goes to restart a farm generator in the fog with a walkie-talkie; the radio voice says don't open the door, the narrator refuses the knocking brother; the radio voice keeps saying 'over', which his brother never says
